name: qwen-inpaint-v0
purpose: Determine whether the bundled Qwen inpainting blueprint can make a localized appearance edit without changing protected pixels or adjacent subject anatomy.
test_case: Change the existing white shirt to royal blue using a shirt-only mask.

result.notes: The model changed the white T-shirt into a blue sports bra/crop top instead of preserving its cut. It created a pale ghosted band across the torso and damaged transitions near the shoulders and waist. The output demonstrates localized generative influence but fails controlled garment replacement.

decision_rule: Pass when masked_instruction_adherence, protected_region_preservation, boundary_quality, and identity_preservation are at least 4 and artifact_severity is at most 2.
conclusion: The bundled four-step Qwen inpainting workflow is not accepted for controlled garment replacement. It may remain useful for unconstrained object removal or region regeneration, but those require separate evaluation.
